<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

To convert a distance from kilometres into miles you can use the following process: 

Start with a number of kilometres

Halve the number and write down your answer

Halve the answer (don't write anything down)

Halve the answer again and write down your answer

Add the two answers you've written down together.

This is the number of miles.

E.g.

$\boxed{Convert\:88\ \text{km}\:into\:miles}$

![papers/city-of-london-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q34-i00.png](/assets/papers/city-of-london-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q34-i00.png "papers/city-of-london-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q34-i00.png")

$88\ \text{km}$ is the same as $55\ \text{miles}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">To convert a distance from kilometres into miles you can use the following process: 
<emptyline>
Start with a number of kilometres
<emptyline>
Halve the number and write down your answer
<emptyline>
Halve the answer (don't write anything down)
<emptyline>
Halve the answer again and write down your answer
<emptyline>
Add the two answers you've written down together.
<emptyline>
This is the number of miles.
<emptyline>
E.g.
<emptyline>
$\boxed{Convert\:88\ \text{km}\:into\:miles}$
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
$88\ \text{km}$ is the same as $55\ \text{miles}$
</code></pre>

**Question**

Jess and Jill share some sweets.

Jill has $\text{six}$ sweets for every $\text{five}$ sweets Jess has.

Jill gives $\text{eight}$ sweets to Jess.

Now, Jill has $\text{four}$ sweets for every $\text{seven}$ sweets Jess has.

How many sweets do the girls have altogether?

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Clara has forgotten the passcode for her phone. She knows it contains the digits $0, 4$ and $9$ and that one digit is repeated. Clara guesses the passcode and receives the following information:

$9004$ - no digits correct 

$4009$ - one digit correct 

$4409$ - two digits correct 

$4990$ - three digits correct

What is her passcode?

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here are some number cards:

$
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 3 }}} \quad
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 9 }}} \quad
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 2 }}} \quad
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 7 }}}
$


You can use each card once to make the number $3927$, like this:

$
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 3 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 9 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 2 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 7 }}}
$

Use the four number cards to make numbers that are as 
close as possible to the numbers written below. Example

$8000 \qquad \longrightarrow
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 7 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 9 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 3 }}}
\boxed{\huge { \text{ 2 }}}
$

You must **not** use the same card more than once in each answer.

$3000 \qquad \longrightarrow
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 7 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 9 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 3 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 2 }}}}
$  

$7000 \qquad \longrightarrow
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 7 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 9 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 3 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 2 }}}}
$   

$3800 \qquad \longrightarrow
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 7 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 9 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 3 }}}}
\boxed{\phantom {\huge { \text{ 2 }}}}
$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Jemima has five cards which are numbered from $1$ to $5$ on one 
side, and have either a square, a circle, a triangle or a star 
drawn on the other side.

She knows that there is at least one card with each 
shape and that the odd numbered cards do not have 
squares on them. Card number $4$ has a circle on it, and 
two cards that have a sum of $6$ both have stars 
on them. 

What shape is on card $3?$

</div>

A Year $6$ class has $30$ pupils. There are $21$ who

**Question**

A wheel has $3$ different colours painted on its rim, red $(R)$, green $(G)$ and yellow $(Y)$.

As it turns, a pattern is left on the ground.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2010/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png")

$Y \ R \ G \ Y \ R \ \ldots$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a game two discs are tossed and the numbers landing 
uppermost are added together.

The red disc has the number $3$ on one side and $5$ on 
the other side; whereas the blue disc has $4$ on one 
side and $7$ on the other.

If they land so that $3$ and $7$ are 
showing, the score is $10$. Write down the other 
possible scores for this game.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

On the planet Arithmetica, the natives have a special sort of 
arithmetic using the symbol $\mho$.

For example, $5 \ \mho \ 3$ means double $5$ then subtract $3$.

So

$
\begin{aligned}
5 \ \mho \ 3 &= 2 × 5 - 3   \\
             &= 10 - 3      \\
             &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>
